title: Deterministic replay, idempotency, compatibility, restore, rollback, and crash recovery
objective: Prove deterministic replay, idempotency, backup and restore, compatibility, migration, rollback, and bounded crash recovery using synthetic non-influencing fixtures.
business_reason: The system must reconstruct prior synthetic decisions exactly and recover safely from duplicate execution, partial failure, schema change, stale snapshots, and rollback before adversarial integration testing can begin.
inputs: OBSERVABILITY-001 canonical lineage, correlation, artifact hashes, and replay identity
CONTRACT-001 versioned schemas and compatibility contracts
synthetic recovery and migration fixtures only
assumptions: all replay inputs and effects remain synthetic
no production storage or backup system is accessed
live permissions and external effects remain false
evaluator: inspect and preserve existing replay and recovery evaluator boundaries
freeze an additive independent evaluator before material implementation
reject replay mismatch, duplicate effect, partial crash, stale snapshot, migration incompatibility, restore mismatch, and rollback failure mutations
known_bad_cases: replay output differs from original output
duplicate execution creates a second effect
partial crash leaves an accepted inconsistent state
restore does not match the bound backup
rollback does not restore the prior accepted version
acceptance: synthetic replay reconstructs byte-identical canonical outputs
partial failures fail closed and resume deterministically
compatibility and migration rules reject unsupported versions
rollback restores the previous accepted version
live permissions and external effects remain false
rollback: Restore the prior schema, reader, and recovery baseline; block incompatible writes and retain the last accepted synthetic snapshot.
stop_budget: Remain synthetic and non-influencing; preserve existing evaluator hashes, keep external effects disabled, and do not claim production durability, disaster recovery, or operational recovery readiness.
